name: <project name, as it appears in text addressed to the user>
repo_root: <absolute path of the repository root, with forward slashes>
code_root: <root of the application code, with a trailing slash>

language.chat: <language of chat, summaries and the documents the method produces>
language.commit: <language of commit messages and changelog entries>

documents.product: <path of the founding document answering the product role: what it does, for whom, why>
documents.brand: <path of the founding document answering the brand role: identity and market>
documents.domain: <path of the founding document answering the domain role: entities, data, interfaces, vocabulary>
documents.stack: <path of the founding document answering the stack role: what it is built with>
documents.architecture: <path of the founding document answering the architecture role: structure and technical choices with their why>

changelog: <path of the log of released versions, or drop this key>

version.field: <the exact spot in that file where the version lives>

paths.studies: <folder of the notes on a technology, one file per technology>
paths.features: <folder holding the working folders, one per problem>
paths.handoffs: <folder of the handoff documents, one per job left to another agent>
paths.review_state: <folder of the run's state outside version control: the review ledger and the worktree pool's registry>

commit.memory_prefix: <prefix of the memory and documentation commit message>

channels.development: <name of the development branch the work lives on, asked at init — e.g. develop>
channels.production: <name of the production branch, a line of releases: the work does not commit there and it advances only by a release; drop this key and the branch guard stays off>

release.source: <folder of the development branch whose content becomes the production tree, where the two sides do not have the same shape — e.g. plugins; drop this key where they do>
never: <paths that never reach production, on top of the method's own footprint — drop this key where there are none>

paths: <a path belonging to the area, usable as a Git pathspec>

run: <the exact line to run, not a description of it>
<the line that compiles, type-checks or lints <FILES> without writing anything>
<the line that applies the safe lint and format fixes to <FILES>>
<the line that runs only the tests <FILES>>
<the lines that produce the area's coverage measurement>
